name: Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.)
origin_detail: Sentry began in 2008 as an unlicensed, 71-line Django plugin written by David Cramer and was published under BSD-3-Clause from 2009. The trademark holder is Functional Software, Inc. The company's founding year, co-founders and HQ were not confirmed in fetched pages.
openness_notes: BSD-3-Clause from 2009. Relicensed to the Business Source License on 2019-11-06 (code becomes Apache-2.0 after 36 months; no offering a commercial version of Sentry's service). On 2023-11-17 Sentry introduced its own Functional Source License (FSL), with a two-year change date to Apache-2.0 or MIT, applied to Sentry and Codecov. SDKs remain open source. Non-OSI today: level 1, but delayed-open by design.

license_history.license: Business Source License (36-month change date to Apache-2.0)
Functional Source License (2-year change date to Apache-2.0 or MIT)

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Pre-emptive: Sentry said cloud resale had 'not yet happened'; motives were funded competitors copying its work and standardizing licences. No fork found.

robustness: Single vendor, but every release becomes Apache-2.0/MIT after two years, so an open fork path is guaranteed by the licence. Sentry also pays upstream maintainers: $1.0M across 132 developers in its 2026 Open Source Pledge report, up from $155,000 in 2021 (self-reported). Over 4 million developers use it (company site).
openness_effect_assessment: Sentry closed pre-emptively, before any cloud provider resold it, then shortened the closed window with FSL. It reports over 4 million developers and no fork appeared, which suggests a SaaS-first product with a delayed-open licence loses little adoption. Financial effects could not be assessed because funding, valuation and revenue were not confirmed.
key_takeaway: Sentry is the architect of the 'delayed open source' middle ground: source-available now, Apache/MIT after two years, paired with direct payments to open-source maintainers ($1M in 2026). It is a third path between OSI licensing and permanent source-available licences, built for a company whose product is mainly consumed as a service.
